content.u0_what_landed: The domain layer of the identity-theorem plan is in body: (1) D = {s | -1 < s.re} is open (IsOpen.preimage continuous_re isOpen_Ioi), convex (a direct weighted-argument proof, no Mathlib convexity machinery needed) and hence connected (Mathlib Convex.isConnected, nonempty witness 2); (2) U = D \ {1} is open (IsOpen.sdiff isClosed_singleton); (3) the path geometry: P(a) = a2c_anchor a = (2, a.im) if a.im != 0 else (2, 1) - the anchor on the vertical line {Re = 2} at nonzero height, with a2c_anchor_in_Dcut (P(a) in U for all a); segment lemmas a2c_segA_in_Dcut (every point of the segment from a to P(a) lies in U - Re by the weighted argument, and p != 1 by the height split: a real forces the segment off the real axis with the endpoint a != 1 as the only height-0 point; a non-real keeps the segment at height a.im != 0) and a2c_segM_in_Dcut (every point of the segment between two anchors lies in U - Re = 2 throughout, height argument for p != 1); (4) a2c_sL_in_Dcut: the band off-points are in U (re = 1/2 - d0 > -1/2 and im = t >= 1000 != 0). Note recorded: Mathlib has NO IsPreconnected.mono (heredity of preconnectedness is genuinely false - counterexample [-1,1] preconnected, {-1,1} not), which is exactly why the direct path construction is the right route; the full preconnectedness theorem (U6) assembles these segments into a JoinedIn path once written.
content.u1u6_what_is_pinned: Every analyticity API the plan needs was verified present in this mathlib checkout before committing to the route: hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_lip (Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntegral.lean:165 - the Leibniz theorem taking hs in nhds x0, integrability of F x0, an integrable bound, per-a local Lipschitz and per-a HasFDerivAt); DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd (CauchyIntegral.lean:631); the full AnalyticOnNhd algebra (add/sub/mul/const_smul/div/smul/comp in Constructions.lean); eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq (Analysis/Analytic/Uniqueness.lean:223 - the identity principle: AnalyticOnNhd on a preconnected set + eventual equality at one point => EqOn); analyticOn_riemannZeta (Mathlib zeta fact on {1}^c); and an in-tree template for exactly this move: Mathlib NumberTheory/Harmonic/ZetaAsymp.lean:477 proves the conjugation identity for riemannZeta on {1}^c by the same eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq pattern. The decomposition of both sides is closed: W-side = riemannZeta (analytic on {1}^c) minus p4_P n (finite sum of s ~- (k+1)^(-s) = exp(-s Log (k+1)), entire) plus p4_I n (n^(-s+1)/(1-s), holomorphic off the pole) - all standard; P4-side = p4_em_expr s n = -1/2 (n)^(-s) + (s/12) n^(-s-1) - 1/2 * INT_{Ioi n} (B2 x) s (s+1) x^(-s-2) dx - all polynomial/power pieces standard except the ONE genuinely new analyticity: the tail integral in s (U1-U4), which is where the new in-body mathematics lives. The integrability domain note: the tail integral converges absolutely exactly where s.re > -1 (integrand ~ x^(-s.re-2), INT x^(-p) converges for p > 1) - matching the domain D exactly, which is why D was chosen.

Lean 4.33.1 lessons from the U0 grind (for future units): (1) 'ring' does NOT use local equalities to close goals - split such steps into pure-identity ring steps + explicit simpa [hab] / rw [hab] steps (probed and confirmed with a minimal counter-example before relying on it); (2) be aware of tactics that silently close (norm_num at he closes on 1 = 0 contradiction); use explicit 'exact (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) ≠ 0) he' style instead; (3) calc steps with tactic proofs are fragile under multi-line continuation in this pipeline - prefer named has + term-mode calc or a by-block per have; (4) the if in 'a2c_anchor' sits under a .re/.im projection, so split_ifs CANNOT see it - by_cases + simp [a2c_anchor, h] is the working pattern (define the anchor with Complex.mk 2 1 / Complex.mk 2 a.im so the projections fold rfl); (5) ((1 - r) * a) ELABORATES AS COMPLEX subtraction when a : ℂ - pin the real coefficient explicitly as ((1 - r : ℝ) * a) or the Complex.re_ofReal_mul / im_ofReal_mul bridges fail with a coercion mismatch; (6) sub_pos.mpr hy gives '0 < y.re - -1' which is NOT definitionally '0 < y.re + 1' - bridge with linarith-derived positivity; (7) Complex.mk + simp [h, Complex.mk] + norm_num is the robust anchor-computation pattern; (8) p in {1} is NOT an equality term - bridge with 'have h1'' : p = 1 := by simpa using h' before congrArg.
